newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Pharmacia to rework Rogaine ads.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Pharmacia to rework Rogaine ads.

text.p: Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc plans to rework the advertising campaign behind Rogaine as part of its drive to dominate the budding hair-growth market, a senior executive said.

Early reaction has indicated consumers want more information about the over-the-counter product and its use, which could lead Pharmacia & Upjohn to use more direct marketing or longer 60-second broadcast advertising spots, Michael Valentino, the company's newly named U.S. consumer healthcare president in an interview Thursday.

"I think we're out there right now at very significant (spending) levels," he said. "What I'm not convinced of yet is that we're out there with the right message, the right look the right information."
He declined to detail advertising spending.
Rogaine was launched over-the-counter in April and Pharmacia & Upjohn expects sales of between $150 to $200 million this year, Valentino said.
Rogaine had U.S. sales of $96 million in 1995, when it required a prescription and sold for twice the OTC price of about $29.
Valentino said Rogaine is being used by one percent of the potential market. But in an effort to expand that penetration, the company needs to recast its marketing effort, he said.
Pharmacia & Upjohn is collecting marketing data and working with its agency, Grey Advertising Inc, to "refine" its Rogaine campaign, he said.

Since the over-the-counter launch, Rogaine has been hit by a host of generic competitors and news others, including pharmaceutical giant Merck and Co Inc, are developing baldness treatments in a bid to tap into the hair-growth market.
About 35 million men and 20 million women in the U.S. are estimated to be losing their hair.
Valentino said generics, sold by companies including Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd, Bausch & Lomb Inc and Alpharma Inc, have not significantly hurt Rogaine sales and have not forced a price cut.

"The way we'll deal with the generics is to continually innovate in the category with new claims, new forms, new packaging, always stay one step ahead," he said. The company has filed for FDA approval for an extra-strength Rogaine.

Valentino did not rule out partnership deals with other firms, including Merck, working in the baldness field in order to maintain a leadership role in the hair-growth business. He said, however, not such talks were underway.
Rogaine is Pharmacia & Upjohn's largest U.S. consumer product, followed by the pain reliever Motrin with U.S. sales of under $100 million a year, Valentino said.

The company has a cholesterol-lowering drug pending FDA approval for switching from prescription to OTC sales. Future prescription-to-OTC switches could come in areas of urinary incontinence, diabetes and acne treatments, he said.
"Based on what I know today, I think the P&U portfolio offers many opportunities" for switches, Valentino said.
